items.title: 67426_Hayes Pillars oral history interview
items.q: Snub Mosley joined the band about a month later. Snub Mosley played trombone. So we worked on that job and we played requests for the people...

ctx.x: Does he still play that slide saxophone?

Oh, yeah. Yeah. He still plays it, yeah. That's one of his features, yeah. And he has a combo. He plays in all the smart clubs and things in, I believe, New York, New Jersey, around. He's well known in musical circles. Snub Mosley.

Of course, James Jeeter was -- James Jeeter, my partner, was the first alto player. He never did play any hot saxophone, but he played first saxophone. Lee Hilliard -- I mentioned him -- Lee Hilliard. There was A. G. Godley who played the drums. A. G. Godley wrote a book on drums. He

items.title: 67426_Hayes Pillars oral history interview
items.q: Snub Mosley that Bosely stuck with the band

ctx.x: We couldn't go any farther. We had a guy in the band named Brent Sparks who contacted a fella who owned a filling station and this man was I believe a Mason. And this man came to the rescue of Brent Sparks and us, we got enough money to get into Cleveland, Ohio. We got back into Cleveland, Ohio and was able to borrow enough money to get us to Syracuse, New York. Jeter was driving a Model A Ford, three of us were riding with him. We had our instruments packed in the back in the rumble seat. The rumble seat could…

So we had been booked into a pocket. And there we were in Syracuse, New York, where no work, and that's when Stuff Smith left the band and went back to Buffalo, where his wife was. A. G. Godley Bartley left the band and went back to Cleveland, where his wife was. So the band almost broke up there in Syracuse, Peanuts Peter Holland stuck with the band, we had the reed section stuck with the band, Snub Mosley that Bosely stuck with the band, Crook, the banjo player, stuck with the band. So Jeter went out and he…

It was a four piece job, Jeter, myself, and the [Eugene] ed. banjo player, Crook, and we borrowed a drummer from somebody else. And we made $15.00 on that job. And that was the best $15.00 I ever made in my life.

items.title: 68098_Snub Mosley oral history interview
items.q: By the time we got to St. Louis Hayes Pillars was in the band.

items.title: 67426_Hayes Pillars oral history interview
items.q: In the brass section, he -- we had Harry Sweets Edison, and Leo Snub Mosley on the trombone.

ctx.x: Cozy Cole. They were just like that. They both were technicians. The same type technician. They were great friends. We had a banjo player named Eugene Crooke in Trent's band. Eugene Crooke was a great banjo player. And he was a tall fellow, thick sideburns. And he and Leo loved each other but they never could get along. They was fighting each other like cats and dogs. They would argue all the time, see, in the band, see. They never fought each other but they just -- they never could get along. But if one was in…
